name: Protocol Handlers
plain: Lets a site or installed app handle links like mailto: or web+music:.
meaning: Opens links with that scheme in the site after the person approves.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Lets a site or installed app handle links like mailto: or web+music:.

limits.headline: Can open links like mailto: in the site after you approve it
limits.user_action: You tap a mailto: or similar link and approve the site as its handler
can: Open that kind of link in the site after you approve
Handle custom link types like web+music:
Ask again if you change your mind in settings
cannot: Take over links without your approval
Work in Firefox for most link types, Safari or on phones
Hijack links from sites you never approved
limits.reach_label: One link type, if you approve
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge on computers ask first. Firefox, Safari and phones do not support it.

story.what_it_is: A site can ask to open links like mailto: or custom web+ links, so clicking them opens that site.

marketing.name: registerProtocolHandler
marketing.pitch: Lets a site or installed app register to handle certain link types, like mail links.

story.for_you: You may see a small prompt asking to let a site open links of one type, such as mail links. If you allow, clicking such a link opens that site. You can change it in browser settings.
story.for_makers: Makers of web mail, chat and calendar apps want to be the default for those links. It makes their web app part of daily flow. It needs an allow, to stop sites from hijacking links.

use_cases.example: Gmail asks to handle mailto links, so clicking an email address anywhere opens a new Gmail draft.
A meeting site registers to open meeting links, so clicking one opens its web app.
A web music player handles a custom music link type, so a shared link starts the song.
A web game launcher handles invite links so a click opens the right game room.
A web calendar app handles calendar links to add events.
A chat web app handles chat invites from messages and web pages.
A malicious site tries to take over mail links to capture drafts. The prompt gives you a chance to refuse.

technical_bounds: Custom schemes must start with web+
